theory.intro: A **population** is every individual we are interested in. A **census** collects data from the whole population. A **sample** collects data from part of the population.
facts: The population is the whole group the investigation is about.
A census collects information from every member of the population.
A sample collects information from only part of the population.
Identify the population from what the investigation wants to find out, then check whether all or only part of that population is included.
steps: Identify the whole population the investigation is about.
Check whether data is collected from every member or only part of that population.
Classify the collection as a census if the whole population is included, or a sample if only part is included.

workedExamples.question_text:
A factory investigates the quality of the $3200$ pens it produced on Monday. Every pen produced that day is inspected.
Identify the population and classify the collection as a census or a sample.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Population: **all $3200$ pens produced by the factory on Monday**.
This is a **census** because every pen in that population is inspected.

workedExamples.question_text:
Scientists investigate the salt content of the water in a river. They collect $600$ mL of water from the river to analyse.
Identify the population and classify the collection as a census or a sample.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Population: **all water in the river**.
This is a **sample** because the $600$ mL collected is only part of the river's water.

workedExamples.question_text:
Researchers investigate the travel habits of all adult residents of a city. They survey every adult resident of one apartment building, containing $120$ adults. Separately, they survey $640$ adults selected across the city. Neither collection includes every adult resident of the city.
Identify the population and classify each collection as a census or a sample.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Population: **all adult residents of the city**.
The apartment-building collection is a **sample** because the building's $120$ adults are only part of the city's adult population.
The citywide collection is also a **sample** because it includes only $640$ adults, rather than every adult resident.

workedExamples.question_text:
An inspector investigates the quality of all pens produced by Factory A on Tuesday and all pens produced by Factory B on Tuesday.
Factory A produced $2800$ pens, and $50$ are inspected. Factory B produced $1900$ pens, and every one is inspected.
Identify the population for each factory and classify each collection as a census or a sample.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Factory A population: **all $2800$ pens produced by Factory A on Tuesday**.
Its collection is a **sample** because only $50$ of those pens are inspected.
Factory B population: **all $1900$ pens produced by Factory B on Tuesday**.
Its collection is a **census** because every pen in that population is inspected.

foundation.question_text:
A school wants information about the heights of its $920$ students. It measures every student.
Identify the population and state whether the collection is a census or a sample.
foundation.solution_text:
Population: **all $920$ students at the school**.
This is a **census** because every student is measured.

foundation.question_text:
A school wants information about the heights of its $920$ students. It measures $60$ randomly chosen students.
Identify the population and state whether the collection is a census or a sample.
foundation.solution_text:
Population: **all $920$ students at the school**.
This is a **sample** because only $60$ students are measured.

foundation.question_text:
A quality inspector weighs $30$ of the $5000$ jars filled by a factory in one day, to check the mean fill of the day's production.
Identify the population and state whether the collection is a census or a sample.
foundation.solution_text:
Population: **all $5000$ jars filled that day**.
This is a **sample** because only $30$ jars are weighed.

foundation.question_text:
A survey investigates the voting intentions of all voters in a state election. It collects information from $750$ randomly chosen voters.
Identify the population and state whether the collection is a census or a sample.
foundation.solution_text:
Population: **all voters in the state election**.
This is a **sample** because only $750$ voters are surveyed.

foundation.question_text:
A factory checks the quality of every bolt produced during April.
Identify the population and state whether the collection is a census or a sample.
foundation.solution_text:
Population: **all bolts produced by the factory during April**.
This is a **census** because every bolt in that population is checked.

foundation.question_text:
A manufacturer investigates the lifetimes of a batch of $2400$ light globes by testing $45$ globes from the batch.
Identify the population and state whether the collection is a census or a sample.
foundation.solution_text:
Population: **all $2400$ light globes in the batch**.
This is a **sample** because only $45$ globes are tested.

foundation.question_text:
A biologist investigates the number of eggs in the nests of a colony. The eggs in every one of the colony's $82$ nests are counted.
Identify the population and state whether the collection is a census or a sample.
foundation.solution_text:
Population: **all $82$ nests in the colony**.
This is a **census** because every nest is included.

Identify the population and state whether the collection is a census or a sample.
development.solution_text:

development.question_text:
An airline wants the mean check-in time of all $18\,400$ passengers it handles in a week.
It times $250$ of them and gets a mean of $6.3$ minutes.
Identify the population and state whether the collection is a census or a sample.
development.solution_text:
Population: **all $18\,400$ passengers handled by the airline that week**.
This is a **sample** because only $250$ passengers are timed.

development.question_text:
An investigation concerns the salaries of all workers in an industry. It records the salary of every employee at one company with $620$ employees. Other companies in the industry are not included.
Identify the population and state whether the collection is a census or a sample.
development.solution_text:
Population: **all workers in the industry**.
This is a **sample** because the company's $620$ employees are only part of that population.

development.question_text:

development.solution_text:
Population: **all $2300$ trees in the plantation**.
This is a **census** because every tree is measured.

development.question_text:

Identify the population and classify each collection as a census or a sample.
development.solution_text:
Population: **all $15$ swimming pools owned by the council**.
The noon collection is a **census** because every pool is measured.
The $5$ pm collection is a **sample** because only $5$ pools are measured.

mastery.question_text:
A health department investigates the sleep habits of all Year $11$ students in a state. It surveys every Year $11$ student at one school, which has $148$ Year $11$ students, and separately surveys $850$ Year $11$ students selected from across the state. Neither collection includes all Year $11$ students in the state.
Identify the population and classify each collection as a census or a sample.
mastery.solution_text:
Population: **all Year $11$ students in the state**.
The school collection is a **sample** because the school's $148$ Year $11$ students are only part of the state's population.
The statewide collection is also a **sample** because it includes only $850$ of the state's Year $11$ students.

mastery.question_text:
A researcher investigates daily podcast listening among all adult residents of a town. The researcher surveys every adult resident in one apartment building, containing $96$ adults. Other adult residents of the town are not surveyed.
Identify the population and state whether the collection is a census or a sample.
mastery.solution_text:
Population: **all adult residents of the town**.
This is a **sample** because the building's $96$ adults are only part of that population, even though every adult in the building is surveyed.

mastery.question_text:
Scientists investigate all $8700$ trees in a forest. They measure every tree in a study area containing $140$ trees, but do not measure the remaining trees in the forest.
Identify the population and state whether the collection is a census or a sample.
mastery.solution_text:
Population: **all $8700$ trees in the forest**.
This is a **sample** because only the $140$ trees in the study area are measured.

mastery.question_text:
An investigation concerns all Brand A batteries produced last year and all Brand B batteries produced last year.
For Brand A, $72$ batteries are tested from a total of $6000$. For Brand B, every one of the $4800$ batteries is tested.
Identify the population for each brand and classify each collection as a census or a sample.
mastery.solution_text:
Brand A population: **all $6000$ Brand A batteries produced last year**. Its collection is a **sample** because only $72$ are tested.
Brand B population: **all $4800$ Brand B batteries produced last year**. Its collection is a **census** because every battery in that population is tested.
